macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Wall Street posts steep losses as AI concerns deepen tech sell-off
items.summary: The S&P 500 fell 1.8%, the Nasdaq Composite dropped 2.9%, and the Dow declined 1.1% in the latest session as investors questioned elevated AI valuations and corporate spending. The Nasdaq’s decline was its worst since June, while Treasury yields fell as investors sought safer assets.

items.title: Amazon gives cautious holiday-quarter outlook despite strong AWS growth
items.summary: Amazon reported weaker-than-expected third-quarter results and issued a cautious sales outlook for the crucial holiday period. AWS revenue grew 39.3% year over year, but investors remained concerned about the scale of the company’s AI-related capital spending.

items.title: Intel plunges after disappointing profit forecast
items.summary: Intel shares suffered their biggest loss since 1974 after the chipmaker issued a profit forecast below analyst expectations, adding to broader investor concerns about the sustainability of the AI-driven technology rally.

items.title: Eurozone economy grows faster than expected in third quarter
items.summary: Eurozone GDP increased 0.4% from the previous quarter, exceeding the 0.2% consensus forecast, while year-over-year growth reached 1.3%. The result indicated moderate resilience despite higher energy prices linked to the Iran conflict.

items.title: ExxonMobil and Chevron beat quarterly estimates
items.summary: Both oil majors reported better-than-expected quarterly results, benefiting from higher energy prices and record production. The energy sector was among the stronger areas of the market as oil prices rose.

items.title: Fed holds benchmark rate steady at 3.75%–4.00%
items.summary: The Federal Reserve left its benchmark interest rate unchanged in a 10–2 vote at its latest meeting. Markets are also preparing for upcoming labor-market data, which could influence expectations for future policy decisions.

items.title: Investors prepare for major earnings and U.S. employment data
items.summary: Markets face a busy week featuring the U.S. employment report and earnings from major technology companies, including Apple. The combination of labor data, election uncertainty, and AI-focused corporate results is expected to shape near-term trading.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin and Ethereum show modest gains
items.summary: Bitcoin was reported at approximately $77,582, up 0.3% over 24 hours, while Ethereum was around $2,255.66, up 0.5%.

items.title: Binance raises coverage for stolen assets to 90%
items.summary: Binance said it has reserved more than $6.34 billion to cover losses from a security incident, raising reported coverage from 80% to 90%. The exchange said withdrawals would resume in phases after completing a reserve snapshot.

items.title: Binance SAFU transfers 7,499 BTC
items.summary: Approximately 7,499 BTC, valued at about $581 million, was transferred from a Binance SAFU wallet to an unidentified address, according to blockchain-monitoring data.

items.title: Kintsu warns of website DNS hijacking
items.summary: Kintsu said its official website was compromised through a domain-registrar issue and warned users not to connect wallets or sign transactions. It advised potentially affected users to revoke authorizations and move assets through a trusted recovery platform.

items.title: Taiwan passes virtual-asset legislation
items.summary: Taiwan’s legislature passed the Virtual Asset Service Act, requiring virtual-asset service providers and stablecoin issuers to obtain approval from the Financial Supervisory Commission. Violations may carry prison terms of up to 10 years.

items.title: Crypto market faces volatility after Binance breach
items.summary: One market report said Bitcoin fell toward $77,400, while about $1.59 billion in leveraged positions were liquidated over 24 hours. Ethereum, BNB, XRP, Solana and Dogecoin were also reported lower in that account.

items.title: Ripple receives approval for U.S. national trust bank
items.summary: Ripple reportedly obtained approval for a U.S. national trust bank, marking a regulatory milestone for its institutional banking strategy.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Sony Bend’s Next Game Reportedly Targets 2027
items.summary: A report says Sony Bend is developing a third-person cooperative game that is not intended as a live-service title. The project may be announced and released in 2027, though details remain unconfirmed.

items.title: John Romero’s Cancelled Xbox Shooter Resumes Development
items.summary: Romero Games has reportedly signed with a new, unnamed publisher to continue development of the previously cancelled shooter. The studio was reduced from roughly 110 employees to five after losing funding in 2025.

items.title: Ubisoft Reorganizes Casual Mobile Games Division
items.summary: Ubisoft is moving several mobile properties, including Kolibri, Ketchapp and Hungry Shark, into a new casual-games arm. The reorganization includes one cancellation and plans to reduce costs by a further €200 million over two years.

items.title: NES Receives New Physical Release Decades After Launch
items.summary: The Angry Video Game Nerd 8-Bit is now available as a physical game for original NES hardware. The title was initially released digitally in 2025.

items.title: Gaming Industry Braces for Grand Theft Auto VI Launch
items.summary: The gaming sector is entering a quieter November as publishers avoid competing directly with Grand Theft Auto VI, scheduled for November 19. The industry is also facing stagnant growth, layoffs, studio closures and consolidation.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI Generates Strong Pre-Launch Demand
items.summary: A report citing Sensor Tower estimates that Grand Theft Auto VI had nearly 7 million pre-orders six weeks before release, generating more than $600 million. A separate survey found that 18% of U.S. workers plan to take launch day off.

items.title: Tomodachi Life Ranks Among 2026’s Biggest New Releases
items.summary: Newzoo data cited by Polygon places Tomodachi Life as the third-highest-revenue new release of 2026 through September across six major Western European and North American markets. It has reportedly outperformed several major releases, including Resident Evil Requiem and Forza Horizon 6.
